sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the southern Capitanata plain, across the lower Ofanto R. valley south of the city of Foggia, and belongs to the oblique to right-lateral strike-slip system that affects the central and southern Adriatic foreland. This source is a near-vertical, ca. N-dipping, fault to the east of the main extensional axis of the southern Apennines.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a sparse intermediate to damaging seismicity in this region, but also the three destructive earthquakes of (from west to east): 17 July 1361 (Mw 6.1, Ascoli Satriano), 20 March 1731 (Mw 6.3, Foggiano), and 11 May 1560 (Mw 5.7, Barletta-Bisceglie).
This Source is thought to be a deep, blind E-W fault system, a part of the tectonic mechanism that seems to characterize the entire seismogenic domain east of the southern Apennines backbone, and possibly of the central ones too. The eastern sector of this source is thought to have caused the 1560 earthquake, while the central one could have caused the destructive 1731 event, and the western one is thought to have caused the complex 1361 earthquake.
Some segments of this Source have been associated with the key earthquakes that have affected this region. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Source in this Database.
The strike of this Source was based on that of the mapped subsurface structures. The dip was based on seismological data and geometrical considerations. The rake represents right-lateral strike slip, based on seismological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on subsurface data. The slip rate was inferred from geodynamic considerations for the tectonic environment that includes this Source.
